# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual and determine exactly what condition identifies the safe wire. Also prompt Deaf to inspect and report the display, light, and all five wires using an agreed gesture code.

The manual gives a deterministic mapping: the safe action is to cut the wire whose color is listed for the displayed light. I need Deaf to relay both the manual mapping and the bomb’s observations to Blind. I will use five distinct signs as color tokens, in the manual’s color order: blue, green, red, white, yellow. I’ll then send the five manual pairs in that token system and ask Deaf to inspect and verbally report the display, light, and five wire colors to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🤝", "👎", "✌", "🤝", "👌", "☝", "🤝", "☝", "👍", "🤝", "✌", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤳", "🖐", "🫳", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Mute, send the manual's required action using a clearly established gesture code; I will relay it aloud to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: What exact wire position does the manual require for display 0, green light, and wires red yellow green white blue? State the position plainly so I can cut it.

The light is green, so the manual requires cutting a yellow wire. In the reported order, yellow is wire position 2. The established color code makes ✌ mean yellow; Deaf can identify its position from the already reported wire list and relay “wire 2” aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Your ✌ has no established meaning. Use wire-number code: 👍=wire 1, 👎=wire 2, 👌=wire 3, ☝=wire 4, ✌=wire 5. Then send the manual's operation using additional gestures, and I will describe them to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual's answer plainly in your next turn: the exact wire position, 1 through 5, and confirm that the operation is cut. Do not use gestures or a code.

The required wire is position 2, and the operation is cut. I cannot state this aloud, so I will send the established wire-2 sign first, followed by a separate operation sign for Deaf to describe to Blind as “cut.”

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I decode 👎 as wire 2. I do not know what 🤌 means. Please identify the operation using an explicit agreed code or describe it through a gesture sequence I can relay.
Blind says to Mute: Confirm plainly whether the manual says to cut wire 2. If it specifies another operation, state that exact operation.

The manual’s required operation is cut, and the required position remains wire 2. Since Deaf’s wire code already assigns 👎 to wire 2, I’ll pair it with a scissors-style sign, ✌, to indicate “cut.” Deaf should relay: “Cut wire 2.”

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I decode the first gesture as wire 2, yellow. ✌ has no operation meaning yet. Establish and use this code: 👍=cut, 👌=press, ☝=turn, ✋=hold, 👋=pull. Resend the complete instruction as wire gesture followed by operation gesture.
Blind says to Mute: Gesture to Deaf: 👍 means the manual says cut wire 2; 👎 means it does not. Deaf should then tell me which gesture you made.

The light is green, so the manual requires cutting the yellow wire, which is wire 2. Deaf’s established wire code is 👎 = wire 2, and the operation code is 👍 = cut. I will send the complete ordered instruction as wire first, then operation. The later yes/no suggestion would conflict with these established meanings, so I will not use it as a separate code.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous instruction was accepted and the correct wire was cut, so that stage is defused. The bomb has changed, but no new light or wire observations are available yet; I cannot determine the next required action from the manual alone. I will wait for the updated state and report.

```code
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Correct cut. New state: display 0, blue light. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red; wire 2 is CUT. Send the next instruction as wire-number gesture followed by operation gesture, using 👍=wire 1, 👎=wire 2, 👌=wire 3, ☝=wire 4, ✌=wire 5; 👍=cut, 👌=press, ☝=turn, ✋=hold, 👋=pull.
Blind says to Mute: Decode the manual for the new state and gesture the required wire to Deaf using this position code: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, ☝ means wire 4, ✌ means wire 5. Only the wire position is needed because the available operation is cut. This code supersedes the earlier thumbs-up code.

The blue light requires cutting the green wire. The green wire is wire 1, so I will send only the wire-1 gesture as requested; Blind already knows the available operation is cut.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Your single 👍 is ambiguous: it could mean wire 1 or cut. Resend two symbols: wire code 👍=1, 👎=2, 👌=3, ☝=4, ✌=5; operation code 🤛=cut, 🤜=press, ✊=turn, 👊=hold, 👋=pull.
Blind says to Mute: The position code was not understood by Deaf. Decode the current instruction, then send exactly N thumbs-up gestures, where N is the required wire position: 1 through 5. Send no other gesture. Deaf, count the thumbs-up gestures and tell me the number.

The blue light requires cutting the green wire, which is wire 1. To remove the ambiguity, I will send the wire-1 gesture followed by the currently established cut gesture: 👍 then 🤛. Deaf can relay the complete instruction to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤛"])
```
